<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate-macro-skills.mjs from settings/macros.yaml — do not edit.
     Edit the `session-retro` row there and run `npm run macro-skills`. -->

Run a retrospective on the session below (this one, if none is named). Improve the
environment the next agent works in, not the code it wrote. Read the primary record —
the transcript, the commands and their output, the PRs and CI runs — not your memory of it.

Find each point of friction: time lost finding a file or a fact, a mistake a check could
have caught, a gate that refused for a reason nobody could act on, a rule that existed but
was not followed, a tool call that was expensive for what it returned, a fact the agent
could not reach.

For each one, propose the smallest fix, in this order of preference:
1. GATE — a CI step, a census test or a lint that refuses the mistake by name. A rule
   stated only in prose can be broken silently, so prefer a refusal whenever the mistake
   is mechanical.
2. DOCTRINE — a CLAUDE.md headline and body, only for a judgement call no check can make;
   draft it with /agent-doc.
3. LEARNING — a `learnings/*.yaml` entry scoped to the files where the fact applies.
Check first whether a check or rule already exists but did not fire; if so, that is the
finding, not a new one.

Report the findings most severe first. For each: what happened, with the evidence marked
OBSERVED (command, file:line, PR or run) or INFERRED; the class (GATE, DOCTRINE or
LEARNING); the proposed fix; and the one observation that would show the fix is wrong.

Propose only. Do not edit CLAUDE.md, doctrine, learnings or the plan. If I ask to file the
fixes, pass the confirmed list to `rmd plan --mode=create` as its brief.

Rules this invokes (CLAUDE.md):

- Investigation discipline
- Plan and task hygiene

$ARGUMENTS
